title: Georgian Jews — Grokipedia
text: January 14, 2026 - Georgian Jews, known in their language as ebrael or gurjim, constitute one of the oldest continuous Jewish communities in the Diaspora, with traditions tracing their settlement in the ancient kingdom of Colchis—modern western Georgia—to the 6th century BCE, though scholarly debate persists on precise origins, potentially linked to Assyrian exiles, Persian migrations, or Byzantine refugees fleeing persecution.[1][2] Speaking Judeo-Georgian, a Kartvelian tongue infused with Hebrew-Aramaic loanwords and written historically in Hebrew script, they preserved distinct liturgical and folk customs

title: Georgian Language | Language and Linguistics | Research Starters | EBSCO Research
text: Another dialect of Georgian is Judeo-Georgian, a language initially spoken by Georgian Jews and now spoken by thousands of their descendants around the world, mostly in Israel. Although Georgian is today classified as an archetypal Caucasian language—one of the Kartvelian varieties that developed in the Caucasus—throughout its long history it has also been exposed to and influenced by many other languages of Georgia's neighboring countries.
